rationale: The core statistics are exactly right for this design: a DESeq2 LRT of ~condition + time + condition:time against ~condition + time with time as a 4-level factor and t0 as reference, followed by per-time-point interaction (difference-in-differences) coefficients with lfcShrink, plus an explicit main-time LRT to quantify the shared trend the question asks to look beyond. QC is concrete (library sizes, VST PCA colored by condition and shaped by time, replicate correlation heatmap), though it only says outliers will be 'confirmed absent' without stating what would be done if one appeared; the filter (>=10 counts in >=3 samples, with genes removed reported) is minimal and matched to group size. Normalization is handled inside DESeq2 with raw counts and VST reserved for QC/clustering, but size factors are never named explicitly. Enrichment is the weakest element: the ORA universe is correctly the filtered gene set and human hallmark/GO-BP are named, but no collection version or gene-set size window is given, and ranking GSEA by an unsigned LRT statistic is a real methodological problem that goes unflagged. Reporting is thorough on design, thresholds, tested/significant counts and honest power caveats, but package versions are not committed to.
